channel.title: Ledger Line
channel.description: Fictional sample stories for offline demos and tests. Not real news: the outlet, the events and the quotes are invented; the places are real so the map can show them.

item.title: Oil prices slide as global demand cools
item.description: Oil prices fell for a third day as traders expect weaker demand this winter. Brent crude dropped 2 percent to 71 dollars a barrel. Refiners say stocks of fuel are higher than usual for the time of year.

item.title: Central bank holds interest rates steady at 3.5 percent
item.description: The central bank has kept interest rates unchanged at 3.5 percent. Policymakers said inflation is easing but they want more evidence before cutting.

item.title: Airline orders 100 new fuel-efficient jets
item.description: A European airline has ordered 100 new short-haul jets in a deal worth about 12 billion dollars. Deliveries will start in 2028.

item.title: North Sea wind farm starts supplying power to 1.2 million homes
item.description: An offshore wind farm in the North Sea has started supplying electricity. The developer says its 140 turbines can power about 1.2 million homes. Power reaches the shore through cables laid along the seabed.

item.title: Shipping costs fall as port congestion eases
item.description: The cost of shipping a container from Shanghai to Rotterdam has fallen by 20 percent in a month. Analysts say congestion at major ports is easing. Fewer ships are now waiting at anchor outside the busiest ports.

item.title: New York stocks close at a record high
item.description: Stock markets in New York closed at a record high on Thursday. Technology shares led the gains, with the main index up 1.4 percent.

item.title: Coffee futures reach a ten-year high after poor harvests
item.description: Coffee prices have climbed to their highest level in ten years after poor harvests in Brazil and Vietnam. Roasters warn shop prices may rise early next year. Dry weather cut the crop on many farms in the hills of Minas Gerais.

item.title: Electric car sales overtake diesel in Europe for the first time
item.description: Sales of fully electric cars overtook diesel cars in Europe last month for the first time, an industry group says. Electric models made up 17 percent of new cars.

item.title: Chocolate makers warn of higher prices as cocoa stays expensive
item.description: Several chocolate makers say they will raise prices again because cocoa remains near record levels. Cocoa has more than doubled in price in two years.

item.title: Tokyo stocks close at a record high led by chipmakers
item.description: Tokyo's main stock index closed at a record high, driven by shares of chipmakers. The index has gained 21 percent since January.

item.title: Lagos shops switch to solar power to cut fuel costs
item.description: Thousands of small shops in Lagos have switched to solar panels to cut fuel costs. A survey found 62 percent of traders now use solar for some of their power.

item.title: BREAKING: Panama Canal reopens after a day-long closure
item.description: The Panama Canal has reopened to ships after fog closed it for a day. The canal authority says about 30 ships are waiting to cross. Shipping companies say the delays should clear within days.

item.title: Rice prices ease in Asia after strong harvests
item.description: Rice prices in Asia have fallen 8 percent since July after strong harvests in Thailand and Vietnam. Traders say supplies look healthy for the rest of the year.

item.title: Small businesses get a new online tool to file taxes
item.description: The tax office has launched a free online tool to help small businesses file their returns. It says the service could save owners several hours each quarter.

item.title: Rail strike halts most trains across Germany
item.description: A 24-hour strike by rail workers has halted most long-distance trains across Germany. The operator says only one in five services is running, and unions say talks over pay have stalled. Many commuters switched to buses and car shares for the day.

item.title: Norway’s central bank raises rates unexpectedly
item.description: Norway’s central bank has raised its main interest rate to 4.75 percent, a move most economists did not expect. The bank said inflation was falling more slowly than it had forecast. The Norwegian krone rose against the euro after the announcement.

item.title: Carmaker to close Turin plant, putting 2,400 jobs at risk
item.description: A carmaker says it will close its plant near Turin by the end of next year. Unions say 2,400 jobs are at risk.

item.title: UK inflation rises unexpectedly to 3.8 percent
item.description: Inflation in the United Kingdom rose to 3.8 percent in September, up from 3.4 percent in August, official figures show. Economists had expected it to stay flat. Food and energy prices drove the rise.
